v-la-brigantine.name: La Brigantine
v-la-brigantine.why: The one thing to learn is Gigaro itself: the peninsula's quiet counter-Pampelonne, a low-key sand-and-pine cove that also serves as the trailhead for the sentier du littoral coastal path out toward the wild capes.
v-la-brigantine.verdict: The rare beach restaurant where the food is not an afterthought, backed by the Lily of the Valley group so the kitchen has real muscle, and warmly rated by critic Pudlowski. Falsifiable claim: chef Charley Bouhier, a Breton, cooks Italian here, and its 2026 season opens on 12 February, far earlier than a typical beach restaurant.
v-la-brigantine.signature: The house focaccia, fresh pasta and Italian-fish plates; it sits on Gigaro, the peninsula's calm western shore, rather than glitzy Pampelonne, so you get the sea and the cooking without the scrum.
v-la-brigantine.caveat: Price and season: beach-restaurant tariffs (roughly 70 to 150 euros a head) for what is, at heart, lunch by the sea; book the sea-front tables, and note it is seasonal.
v-la-brigantine.hook: Feet-near-the-sand Italian on the quiet Gigaro beach, cooked by a Breton chef who takes his pasta seriously.

signal_chip.label: PRAISED BY GILLES
signal_chip.full: Warmly reviewed by critic Gilles Pudlowski; part of the Lily of the Valley group

v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.name: La Brigantine — Lily of the Valley beach club
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.short: La Brigantine — Lily of the Valley beach club
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.why: Where the Gigaro sand runs out into the umbrella pines, the Lily of the Valley drops a table to sea level and cooks Italy — from the northern lakes down to Sicily — beside a wood-fired oven.
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.address: Plage de Gigaro, 83420 La Croix-Valmer, France — the Lily of the Valley beach club at the pine-backed eastern end of Gigaro beach
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.verdict: Go for the setting and the Italian carte, not a rating it doesn't hold: La Brigantine has no star or score of its own. It's the sand-level Italian sibling of the Philippe Starck-designed Lily of the Valley hotel, cooking the peninsula's regions from the northern lakes to Sicily — wood-fired pizzas, guanciale spaghetti, saffron risotto with gambas, grilled sea bass. The kitchens are now run by Charley Bouhier, the "dynamic Breton" who took over after founding executive chef Vincent Maillard — to whom Gault&Millau still credits the hotel's 13/20 gastronomic table Vista — reportedly decamped to Saint-Barth (Pudlowski, 2023). Both Gilles Pudlowski and Jacques Gantié reviewed La Brigantine and called its opening summers a success. Expect beach-club prices: pizzas €19–36, à la carte roughly €70–150 (Pudlowski, 2023; earlier menus ran from the mid-€40s). Falsifiable: if you arrive expecting a gastronomic destination rather than a very good beach kitchen with a serious house behind it, you'll feel the gap.
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.signature: Wood-fired pizza on a program coached by John Bergh, a French pizza champion who consulted on it (Gantié, 2021) — Pudlowski singles out the thin courgette-flower pizza with burrata and ricotta; Gantié the farinata (chickpea) base with mortadella.
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.caveat: This is a scene as much as a kitchen: a Philippe Starck-designed beach club turning 600–800 covers a day (Gantié) at beach-club prices, open in season only — the 2026 listing runs late May to early November, and it's in full summer service now. Gantié, who liked it, still flagged the guanciale spaghetti as over-salted on his visit. Note the chef change: the Gault&Millau 13/20 belongs to the sibling gastronomic table Vista and is still credited by G&M to founding chef Vincent Maillard, but the kitchens are now led by Charley Bouhier.
v-la-brigantine-lily-of-the-vall.person: Charley Bouhier — the "dynamic Breton" chef de cuisine now leading the Lily of the Valley kitchens (La Brigantine and the sibling Vista), per Pudlowski (2023). Founding executive chef Vincent Maillard — trained under Ducasse (Louis XV) and Guy Savoy, still credited by Gault&Millau — reportedly moved to Saint-Barth. John Bergh, a French pizza champion, consulted on the pizza program (not daily staff).

signal_chip.label: Sibling of Vista, G&M 13/20
signal_chip.full: La Brigantine holds no independent Michelin star or Gault&Millau score. Its signal is the house: it shares the Lily of the Valley kitchen team with the hotel's gastronomic table Vista, which carries Gault&Millau 13/20 (2 toques, 2026, listed under the hotel name). G&M still credits that score to founding chef Vincent Maillard, though the kitchens are now led by Charley Bouhier. Separately, La Brigantine itself was reviewed and praised by critics Gilles Pudlowski and Jacques Gantié (2021).
signal_chip.cosign: Gault&Millau 13/20, 2 toques, 2026 — the sibling gastronomic table Vista (founding chef Vincent Maillard; kitchens now led by Charley Bouhier)

v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.name: L'Auberge de l'Oumede
v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.why: L'Auberge de l'Oumede is a small Provencal charm-residence set in the vineyards of Ramatuelle, a short drive from the Pampelonne beaches and Saint-Tropez, prized above all for its calm and its vine-facing terrace about 2 km from the beach. The real thing to learn: on this peninsula, a genuinely quiet table in high summer is scarcer and arguably more valuable than an ambitious one. Verified fact: for 2026 it opens daily from 1 May to 4 October.
v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.verdict: Honesty by negation: the appeal here is the setting, a small Provencal auberge among the vines with a terrace, pool and real quiet, and the food is good rather than transcendent. Falsifiable claim: it opens only for the season, daily from 1 May to 4 October 2026.
v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.signature: The Provencal dinner on the vineyard terrace at dusk; come for the setting and a bottle of local Cotes de Provence rose rather than any single show-stopping dish.
v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.caveat: Honest value warning: several guests find the cooking good-not-exceptional for the prices (starters 30 euros-plus, mains 50 euros-plus). Seasonal, book ahead, and remember it is really a small hotel that also serves dinner.
v-l-auberge-de-l-oumede.hook: A hushed vineyard hideaway in the Ramatuelle vines, minutes from Pampelonne but a world away from the noise.

signal_chip.full: Small vineyard auberge; open daily 1 May to 4 October 2026; mixed value reviews
